subject: B
topic: Political & Physical Divisions of World & India

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The total number of continents in the world is:
questions.explanation: There are 7 continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Australia/Oceania. 5 is the number of oceans. 6 and 8 are incorrect counts.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which is the largest continent in the world by both area and population?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent covering about 44.58 million km² (30% of Earth's land) and home to about 4.7 billion people (60% of world population). Africa is second largest by area. North America is third. Europe is sixth by area.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the physical divisions of India:

(i) The Himalayas form the northern mountain boundary of India.
(ii) The Indo-Gangetic Plain is formed by alluvial deposits of rivers like the Ganga, Yamuna, and Brahmaputra.
(iii) The Deccan Plateau is a triangular plateau bounded by the Western and Eastern Ghats.
(iv) The Thar Desert is located in eastern India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Himalayas stretch across India's northern frontier. (ii) is correct — the Indo-Gangetic Plain is one of the world's largest alluvial plains. (iii) is correct — the Deccan Plateau is a triangular tableland. (iv) is wrong — the Thar Desert is in WESTERN India (Rajasthan), not eastern India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India is divided into how many states and Union Territories (as of 2024)?
questions.explanation: After the reorganisation of J&K in 2019, India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories. 29 States was the count before J&K's reorganisation. 28 States and 9 UTs overcounts UTs. 30 States and 6 UTs is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is described as a subcontinent.
Reason (R): India has a vast geographical diversity — from the highest mountains (Himalayas) to coastal plains, deserts to rainforests, and a large landmass distinct from the rest of Asia.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Indian subcontinent is a well-recognised geographical term. (R) is correct — the vast diversity and distinct landmass (separated by the Himalayas from the rest of Asia) justify the term 'subcontinent'. (R) explains (A) by describing the features that make India qualify as a subcontinent.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following physical features of India with their locations:

Column I:
(a) Western Ghats
(b) Eastern Ghats
(c) Indo-Gangetic Plain
(d) Deccan Plateau

Column II:
(i) Between the two Ghats in peninsular India
(ii) Along the western coast from Gujarat to Kerala
(iii) Northern India from Punjab to Assam
(iv) Along the eastern coast — discontinuous

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Western Ghats run along the western coast (ii). Eastern Ghats are along the eastern coast and are discontinuous (iv). Indo-Gangetic Plain stretches across northern India (iii). Deccan Plateau lies between the two Ghats (i). Option 2 swaps Western and Eastern Ghats. Option 3 swaps Eastern Ghats and Indo-Gangetic Plain. Option 4 swaps Western Ghats and Deccan Plateau.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following countries share a land border with India?

(i) Pakistan
(ii) China
(iii) Bangladesh
(iv) Sri Lanka

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: India shares land borders with Pakistan (west), China (north), and Bangladesh (east), plus Nepal, Bhutan, and Myanmar. Sri Lanka (iv) is separated from India by the Palk Strait — it does NOT share a land border, only a maritime boundary.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The largest ocean in the world is:
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest, covering about 165.25 million km² (about one-third of Earth's surface). The Atlantic is the second largest. The Indian Ocean is third. The Arctic Ocean is the smallest of the major oceans.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the political divisions of the world:

(i) There are approximately 195 recognised sovereign countries in the world.
(ii) The United Nations has 193 member states.
(iii) Africa has the most number of countries among all continents.
(iv) Europe has only 5 countries.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — 195 sovereign states (193 UN members + 2 observers: Vatican City and Palestine). (ii) is correct — 193 member states in the UN. (iii) is correct — Africa has 54 countries, the most of any continent. (iv) is wrong — Europe has approximately 44-50 countries (depending on definitions), not just 5.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The standard meridian of India (82°30'E) passes through which city?
questions.explanation: The Indian Standard Meridian (82°30'E longitude) passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh (near Allahabad/Prayagraj), which is why IST is based on this longitude. Delhi is approximately at 77°E. Mumbai is at about 72°E. Chennai is at about 80°E.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Himalayas are called 'young fold mountains'.
Reason (R): The Himalayas were formed relatively recently (geologically) by the collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate, and they are still rising.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Himalayas are classified as young fold mountains. (R) is correct — they formed about 50 million years ago by plate collision and are still growing (~5mm/year). (R) explains (A) because the recent formation and ongoing tectonic activity is what makes them 'young' in geological terms.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states at approximately 1,600 km. Maharashtra is second with about 720 km. Andhra Pradesh has about 974 km. Tamil Nadu has about 1,076 km. Gujarat's long coastline includes the Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian states with their capitals:

Column I:
(a) Madhya Pradesh
(b) Karnataka
(c) Assam
(d) Rajasthan

Column II:
(i) Jaipur
(ii) Dispur
(iii) Bhopal
(iv) Bengaluru

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh's capital is Bhopal (iii). Karnataka's capital is Bengaluru (iv). Assam's capital is Dispur (ii). Rajasthan's capital is Jaipur (i). Option 2 swaps MP and Karnataka. Option 3 swaps Karnataka and Assam. Option 4 swaps MP and Rajasthan.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the physical features of the world:

(i) Mount Everest (8,848.86 m) is the highest peak in the world.
(ii) The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is the deepest point on Earth.
(iii) The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.
(iv) The Amazon River is the longest river in the world.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Everest at 8,848.86 m is the highest. (ii) is correct — Mariana Trench (~11,034 m deep) is the deepest oceanic point. (iii) is correct — Sahara (~9.2 million km²) is the largest hot desert. (iv) is wrong — the NILE is generally considered the longest river (~6,650 km); the Amazon is the second longest but has the largest volume/drainage basin.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram. Karnataka is in peninsular India, south of the Tropic of Cancer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's island territories:

(i) The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in the Bay of Bengal.
(ii) Lakshadweep is a group of coral islands in the Arabian Sea.
(iii) The southernmost point of India (Indira Point) is in the Nicobar Islands.
(iv) Both island territories are part of the Deccan Plateau.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Andaman & Nicobar are in the Bay of Bengal. (ii) is correct — Lakshadweep consists of coral atolls in the Arabian Sea. (iii) is correct — Indira Point (Great Nicobar) is India's southernmost point. (iv) is wrong — the island territories are NOT part of the Deccan Plateau; they are oceanic islands formed by tectonic activity (Andaman) and coral formation (Lakshadweep).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indo-Gangetic Plain is one of the most fertile regions in the world.
Reason (R): The plain is formed by alluvial deposits brought by the Ganga, Indus, and Brahmaputra river systems over millions of years.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Indo-Gangetic Plain supports intensive agriculture for hundreds of millions of people. (R) is correct — alluvial deposits from major rivers have created extremely fertile soil. (R) explains (A) because the alluvial deposits are precisely what makes the soil so productive.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are landlocked countries (no coastline)?

(i) Nepal
(ii) Bhutan
(iii) Bangladesh
(iv) Afghanistan

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Nepal (i), Bhutan (ii), and Afghanistan (iv) are all landlocked — they have no coastline or direct access to the sea. Bangladesh (iii) is NOT landlocked — it has a coastline along the Bay of Bengal (about 580 km).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: India's total area is approximately __________ million sq km, making it the 7th largest country in the world.
questions.explanation: India's total area is approximately 3.287 million sq km (≈3.3 million sq km), making it the 7th largest country. 2.2 million is too small (that's about Algeria). 2.8 million is closer to Kazakhstan. 4.0 million would exceed India's size significantly.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The six major physical divisions of India are:
options: Northern Mountains, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Coastal Plains, Islands, and Desert
Northern Mountains, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Coastal Plains, Islands, and Thar Desert
Himalayas, Indo-Gangetic Plain, Peninsular Plateau, Coastal Plains, Islands, and Indian Desert
All options describe the same six divisions
questions.correctAnswer: All options describe the same six divisions
questions.explanation: India's six major physiographic divisions are: (1) The Northern Mountains (Himalayas), (2) The Northern Plains (Indo-Gangetic Plain), (3) The Peninsular Plateau (Deccan), (4) The Coastal Plains, (5) The Islands, and (6) The Indian Desert (Thar). All three options list the same six divisions using different names — they are all correct descriptions.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the political map of the world:

(i) Russia is the largest country in the world by area.
(ii) Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.
(iii) China has the largest population in the world.
(iv) Canada is the second largest country by area.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Russia (17.1 million km²) is the largest. (ii) is correct — Vatican City (0.44 km²) is the smallest. (iv) is correct — Canada (10 million km²) is second largest. (iii) is wrong — as of recent years, India has surpassed China as the world's most populous country.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian geographical features with their descriptions:

Column I:
(a) K2 (Godwin-Austen)
(b) Kanchenjunga
(c) Nanda Devi
(d) Anamudi

Column II:
(i) Highest peak in South India (Western Ghats, Kerala)
(ii) Highest peak in India (PoK)
(iii) Third highest peak in the world (Sikkim border)
(iv) Highest peak entirely within India (Uttarakhand)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: K2 is the highest peak in Indian territory (in PoK) at 8,611 m (ii). Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is the third highest peak in the world, on the India-Nepal border in Sikkim (iii). Nanda Devi (7,816 m) is the highest peak entirely within India's borders in Uttarakhand (iv). Anamudi (2,695 m) is the highest peak in South India in the Western Ghats of Kerala (i).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India extends from approximately __________ in the north to __________ in the south (latitude).
questions.explanation: India extends from about 8°4'N (Kanyakumari, mainland; 6°45'N including Indira Point) to 37°6'N (northernmost point in Ladakh). 10°N to 40°N is slightly off. 5°N is too far south. 15°N misses all of South India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Union Territories of India?

(i) Delhi
(ii) Chandigarh
(iii) Goa
(iv) Puducherry

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Delhi (NCT), Chandigarh, and Puducherry are Union Territories. Goa (iii) is NOT a UT — it has been a full state since 1987 (became India's 25th state). The other UTs include Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, J&K, and Ladakh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's neighbours:

(i) India shares its longest land border with Bangladesh.
(ii) Pakistan borders India to the west and northwest.
(iii) Myanmar borders India to the east.
(iv) India shares borders with a total of 9 countries.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — India-Bangladesh border (~4,096 km) is India's longest. (ii) is correct — Pakistan is to the west/northwest. (iii) is correct — Myanmar borders India's northeast. (iv) is wrong — India shares land borders with 7 countries (Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Afghanistan), not 9.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The largest state of India by area is:
questions.explanation: Rajasthan (342,239 km²) is India's largest state by area. Madhya Pradesh (308,252 km²) is second. Maharashtra (307,713 km²) is third. Uttar Pradesh (240,928 km²) is the most populous but fourth in area.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following world regions with their primary political groupings:

Column I:
(a) European Union
(b) ASEAN
(c) SAARC
(d) African Union

Column II:
(i) South Asian countries
(ii) Southeast Asian countries
(iii) European countries
(iv) African countries

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: EU is a grouping of European countries (iii). ASEAN groups Southeast Asian nations (ii). SAARC groups South Asian countries (i). African Union encompasses African nations (iv). Option 2 swaps EU and ASEAN. Option 3 swaps ASEAN and SAARC. Option 4 swaps EU and AU.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the areas of the five largest countries:

| Country | Area (million km²) |
|---------|--------------------|
| Russia | 17.1 |
| Canada | 10.0 |
| USA | 9.8 |
| China | 9.6 |
| Brazil | 8.5 |

Approximately how many times larger is Russia than India (3.3 million km²)?
questions.explanation: Russia/India = 17.1/3.3 ≈ 5.18 ≈ about 5 times. 'About 3 times' is too low. 'About 4 times' is also too low. 'About 6 times' slightly overestimates.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the length of India's borders with neighbouring countries:

| Country | Border Length (km) |
|---------|--------------------|
| Bangladesh | 4,096 |
| China | 3,488 |
| Pakistan | 3,323 |
| Nepal | 1,751 |
| Myanmar | 1,643 |

Which two countries together account for more than 50% of India's total land border shown above?
questions.explanation: Total border shown = 4,096+3,488+3,323+1,751+1,643 = 14,301 km. Bangladesh + China = 4,096+3,488 = 7,584 km = 53% (>50%). Bangladesh + Pakistan = 7,419 = 51.9% (also >50% but slightly less). China + Pakistan = 6,811 = 47.6% (<50%). Pakistan + Nepal = 5,074 = 35.5% (<50%). Bangladesh and China together exceed 50% most clearly.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Peninsular Plateau of India:

(i) It is one of the oldest landmasses on Earth, part of the ancient Gondwanaland.
(ii) It is composed mainly of igneous and metamorphic rocks.
(iii) The plateau is generally higher in the west and slopes eastward.
(iv) The Western Ghats are lower in elevation than the Eastern Ghats.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Deccan Plateau is part of the ancient Gondwana supercontinent. (ii) is correct — it's composed of basalt (igneous from Deccan Traps), granite, and gneiss (metamorphic). (iii) is correct — the plateau tilts from west (higher, near Western Ghats) to east (lower, towards Eastern Ghats). (iv) is wrong — the Western Ghats are HIGHER (average 900-1600m, peak 2,695m at Anamudi) than the Eastern Ghats (average 600m).
